title: Open multiplication for transverse smooth closed subgroups
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $H,K\hookrightarrow G$ be smooth closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. For any group scheme $J$ write $\operatorname{Lie}(J)=T_eJ$ for its tangent space at the identity; identify the tangent spaces of $H$ and $K$ with their images in $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. Suppose $H\cap K=1$ as subgroup functors on all commutative $k$-algebras and that addition is an isomorphism of vector spaces
$$\operatorname{Lie}(H)\oplus\operatorname{Lie}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Lie}(G).$$
Then multiplication $H\times_k K\to G$, $(h,k)\mapsto hk$, is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Neither $G$, $H$ nor $K$ is assumed connected.

source.place: Theorem 13.33 proof of (d), printed p.266: multiplication is injective as a functor, its differential is an isomorphism, and the orbit map identifies its source with an open subscheme. The statement isolates the general transverse-subgroup criterion used in that argument.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The affine quotient description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], applied to the affine open $G$ itself, gives $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $K=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $A=C/I$, $B=C/J$. Since $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] shows that $k\to A$ and $k\to B$ are smooth ring maps; in particular $A$ and $B$ are finitely presented, hence finitely generated, $k$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $H\times_kK=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$ with projections induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; the elements $a_i\otimes1,1\otimes b_j$ from finite generating sets of $A$ and $B$ generate $A\otimes_kB$, so $H\times_kK$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], applied to $k\to B$ along $k\to A$, makes $A\to A\otimes_kB$ smooth, and its composition clause makes $k\to A\otimes_kB$ smooth; by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] again, $H\times_kK\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. Since $G$ is smooth of finite type by hypothesis, both source and target of multiplication are smooth finite-type $k$-schemes.

source.place: Tags 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); elementary finite-generation calculation on the affine product.

proof.text: Let $R$ be any commutative $k$-algebra. If $hk=h\prime k\prime$ in $G(R)$, then $(h\prime)^{-1}h=k\prime k^{-1}$ lies in $H(R)\cap K(R)$, which is $\{1\}$ by hypothesis. Hence $h=h\prime$ and $k=k\prime$. This uses the subgroup inclusions on $R$-points [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], including nonreduced $R$. Thus multiplication is injective on all affine $k$-scheme tests. For any $k$-scheme $T$, two maps $T\to H\times_kK$ with equal composites agree on every affine open of $T$ by that calculation, and therefore agree as scheme morphisms. For an arbitrary scheme test with equal composites, those composites give the same map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so it reduces to a $k$-scheme test. Multiplication is a monomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(d), proof, printed p.266: trivial intersection as functors implies injectivity.

proof.text: Under the projection identification $T_{(e,e)}(H\times_kK)=T_eH\oplus T_eK$ of [lem-sc-product-tangent-space-direct-sum], the tangent map of $H\times K\to G\times G$ is the pair of the inclusion tangent maps: this follows by composing with the two projections, using the tangent map as composition on dual-number maps [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Now [lem-sc-group-addition-tangent-differential], whose group law is written additively but need not be commutative, says the tangent map of multiplication on $G$ sends $(v,w)$ to $v+w$. Consequently $dm_{(e,e)}$ is exactly the addition isomorphism in the hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(d), proof, printed p.266: multiplication induces an isomorphism on identity tangent spaces.

proof.text: Fix $(h,k)\in H(k)\times K(k)$. Define the scheme automorphisms $a(u,v)=(hu,vk)$ on $H\times K$ and $b(g)=hgk$ on $G$. Their inverses use $h^{-1},k^{-1}$, and the group axioms [def-sc-group-scheme] give the identity $m\circ a=b\circ m$ on all algebra-valued points, hence as scheme morphisms. The automorphism $a$ sends $(e,e)$ to $(h,k)$ and $b$ sends $e$ to $hk$. Differentiation is composition on dual-number maps [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], so $dm_{(h,k)}\,da_{(e,e)}=db_e\,dm_{(e,e)}$; differentiating the inverse identities shows $da,db$ are invertible. Step 3 now makes $dm_{(h,k)}$ invertible. The product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies all rational points of $H\times_kK$ with such pairs. No connectedness or conjugation-stability assumption is used.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(d), printed p.266: orbit-map argument; explicit left H and right K translation identities.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-tangent-isomorphism-etale] to $m:H\times_kK\to G$: the field is algebraically closed, step 1 verifies smoothness and finite type, and step 4 verifies the differential condition at every rational point, including every component. Thus $m$ is etale. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is flat and locally of finite presentation. Together with the monomorphism of step 2 these are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open], which proves that $m$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open), implication (3) implies (1); Milne printed p.267 for the smooth tangent criterion.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 13.33(d), printed p.266, general transverse-subgroup form; identity differential and explicit translations followed by the Stacks etale-monomorphism criterion.

lean.statement: theorem isOpenImmersion_transverse_subgroup_product (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G H K : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H] [GrpObj K] [IsAffine G.left] [Smooth G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (i : H ⟶ G) (j : K ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] [IsClosedSubgroupScheme j] [Smooth H.hom] [Smooth K.hom] (hinter : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (h : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R))) ⟶ H) (t : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R))) ⟶ K), h ≫ i = t ≫ j → h ≫ i = 1) (hLie : ∀ v : schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom (GrpObj.onePoint G), ∃! w : schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom (GrpObj.onePoint G) × schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom (GrpObj.onePoint G), (∃ a : Spec (.of (DualNumber (G.left.residueField (GrpObj.onePoint G)))) ⟶ H.left, a ≫ i.left = w.1.val) ∧ (∃ b : Spec (.of (DualNumber (G.left.residueField (GrpObj.onePoint G)))) ⟶ K.left, b ≫ j.left = w.2.val) ∧ w.1 + w.2 = v) : IsOpenImmersion ((i ⊗ₘ j) ≫ μ[G]).left
lean.note: The Lie direct-sum isomorphism is expressed equivalently as unique decomposition of ambient identity tangent vectors into the two subgroup images; image membership is factorization through the subgroup inclusion. No new tangent-space or group-scheme definition.
